text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

An all-women panel that selected a woman over another woman tells you nothing about sex bias — both candidates shared the same sex, so it can't explain why one was preferred. Raising it would likely read as grasping, and would weaken your credibility on the issue that actually matters.

What's worth pursuing is the substance: the successful candidate has roughly half your experience, and the stated differentiator is "client relationships." That's a legitimate criterion for a group-head role, but it's also vague enough to warrant scrutiny.

The real grievance is procedural: two weeks' silence on a written request. Send a polite follow-up, copying HR, citing the original date. Age, not sex, is the more plausible angle if any.
